# Native Whisper and Parakeet evidence

Reference app: unchanged Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`, using `onnx-asr` 0.12.0, CPU ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 and GPU ONNX Runtime 1.26.0. Imported application/resource files, including the GPU requirements, were checked against the release commit. Ten imported `onnx-asr` source/data files were checked against its size/SHA-verified wheel; the reference CPU library matches the independently extracted verified native library exactly. The released GPU installer ran in disposable storage with its unchanged hash-locked wheels. Collection helpers remain outside the maintained tree under ignored task scratch.

`released-frontends.json` and paired compressed PCM/features freeze 22 independent NumPy cases and all 2,017,792 feature values. They cover zero-length/silent audio, 1/159/160/161/319/320/511/512-frame boundaries, impulses, deterministic noise through the full 25-second block and the public English/Chinese clips used by [Qwen's examples](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/README.md). Files carry decompressed size/SHA checks. Native dimensions, valid lengths, masking and finite/NaN/infinite classification must match; finite feature values permit at most `1e-5` absolute difference. The explicitly observed maximum is `2.6226044e-6` for NeMo and `2.3841858e-7` for Whisper on this x86-64 machine. These bounds cover FFT/float arithmetic differences; they are not a transcript-quality metric. Short NeMo inputs deliberately retain the reference normalization behavior instead of hiding its NaNs.

`released-tokens.json` freezes the unchanged decoder's outputs for every individual vocabulary ID (51,865 Whisper and 8,193 Parakeet) plus 600 deterministic combinations per model. The aggregate single-token digests include each ID and output-byte length before its text; combination hashes and character counts catch joined multibyte UTF-8, leading spaces, special tokens and Unicode word/space behavior. Vocabulary archives are unchanged model data with lossless gzip compression, not Python implementations. [Tokenizer notices](tokenizer-NOTICE.md) record their sources and licenses; keep these test fixtures out of installed packages.

`released-onnx-inference.json` freezes eight actual released CPU recognitions: Whisper English automatic/forced, Chinese automatic/forced and doubled English; Parakeet English automatic/forced and doubled English. The longer 30.1025-second input exercises real 25-second splitting and joined output. The native public local-speech factory and its owned `mluva-asr-worker` match every final text SHA/character count and every released metadata field using genuine pinned native ONNX libraries and models. External `/proc` observations verify weight retention, explicit close/reaping and a successful cold restart. Cancelling actual loading interrupts the worker within the check's two-second bound, rejects late output and removes owned resources. The first earlier kernel comparison rejected an incorrect Parakeet int64 target/length input; the corrected worker uses the model's actual int32 tensors and passes.

`released-onnx-cuda-inference.json` freezes the same eight requests through the unchanged CUDA client, with separate released outputs and provider metadata. Its SHA-256 is `0d8123690db06179af02497e983237ca579d52200d5d390dbda00cc530b86fd8`. Both released workers had independently observed NVIDIA compute contexts. The native public factory matches every final text SHA/character count and metadata field on the physical RTX A1000 Laptop GPU. An external `nvidia-smi` observation finds each owned native worker PID with nonzero allocated GPU memory; selecting a device flag alone cannot pass this check. Retention, explicit close/reaping, cold restart and actual loading cancellation pass for both models. Private mode-0700 shader caches disappear before close/cancel returns. Across CPU/CUDA, these tests compare all sixteen frozen results plus four cold-restart results and interrupt four real loading processes.

Both ignored physical tests were explicitly executed successfully. They require `MLUVA_ONNX_ASSETS` pointing to a separately prepared public asset store with `native-runtime/xdg-data/mluva/onnx-runtime/cpu/lib/`, `native-runtime/xdg-data/mluva/gpu-runtime/` and per-model `<id>/xdg-data/mluva/models/<id>-<revision-prefix>/` directories. The native production installer prepared both runtime stores and both model stores. Before inference, the checks independently verify every required model/native-library size and SHA and copy only those artifacts into disposable owner-only storage. The CUDA check additionally verifies all 34 installed native libraries/notices and the absence of other runtime files. Input PCM comes from frozen public fixtures and is WAV-encoded natively. Source collection uses a read-only host view with writable task-owned storage; native shader caches are private. No installed cache is used for inference or changed; no microphone, cloud inference, provider account, credentials or desktop input is used.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p mluva-asr
cargo test --locked -p mluva-asr --test inference \
  actual_cpu_whisper_and_parakeet_match_released_recognition \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p mluva-asr --test inference \
  actual_cuda_whisper_and_parakeet_match_released_recognition \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

This is same-machine/component evidence on an i7-12700H, not complete local-speech or application acceptance. [Native ONNX provisioning evidence](../../../mluva-providers/tests/fixtures/onnx-runtime-evidence.md) covers artifact installation and its cleanup. [Native client evidence](../../../mluva-providers/tests/fixtures/local-asr-evidence.md) covers 230 independent process/protocol sessions, request-abort recovery, concurrent cancellation and four independently collected actual deadline/RSS failures through controlled workers. Broader real languages/audio, empty/malformed WAV process behavior, cancellation during active real inference, production parent-crash cleanup, the worker's CPU address-space limit, controller/UI/Live integration and final distribution remain required. The worker declares a parent-death signal; that declaration alone is not independent production crash evidence. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0, Python removal is pending and no performance improvement is claimed from debug-mode component checks or single GPU-memory observations.

4 October 2026 follow-up: the original component checkpoint above predates the [authorized 2.0.0 cutover](../../../../docs/verification/rust-cutover/README.md). The [released performance record](../../../../docs/verification/rust-release-performance/README.md#whisper-tiny-and-parakeet-client-measurements) now adds 56 public-client sessions/280 actual CPU/CUDA recognitions with exact frozen text/metadata, owned physical GPU contexts and normal reaping/cache cleanup. One excluded warmup plus six measured sessions per model/device/implementation show first recognition about 0.4–0.5 seconds sooner in native, with overlapping resident-English ranges and no general decoder-speed claim. Four complete application checks additionally match paced CPU Dictation final frames, persisted History and retained WAV/UTC filenames for both models. These use the prepared filename-repaired native bundle; installed/published 2.0.0 remains unchanged. Active real inference cancellation/crash/limit behavior, every transient preview/Live state, broader languages and physical/platform acceptance remain open. No frozen model output or maintained Python helper is added.
